rules.name: Acting line, not the header
rules.statement: A code link claiming an action must name the acting line, never a definition, an import or a comment.
rules.risk: A reader follows the link and lands on a heading instead of the work.

sites.why: Refuses every line shape that can never act.
Reports each stored link sitting on a line that cannot act.
Tells the map builder to link the write, call or enforce line itself.

rules.name: One line, or a stated absence
rules.statement: A decision's evidence is exactly one numbered line, or a note saying no single line enforces the decision.
rules.risk: Evidence naming a whole file cannot be checked, so nobody can prove the decision wrong.

sites.why: Refuses evidence that names no line and does not declare the absence.
Refuses evidence that names a line and also declares there is none.
Refuses evidence naming only a file, with no line number.
Repeats the same refusal when the whole map is checked, not one piece.
States that a decision's link is the one link whose line number is required.

rules.name: Two kinds of code link
rules.statement: Only a link claiming an action fires there is checked against the line. A link showing where a thing is defined is not.
rules.risk: Correct links to definitions would be reported as wrong, drowning the real findings.

sites.why: Skips a relation the definition heading itself declares, like one type extending another.
Includes a decision's own line, the strongest claim in the map that a line acts.
Skips a link into a written document, where no line acts.

rules.name: Wrong link, warning only
rules.statement: A code link on the wrong line is only a warning, because the claim it carries can still be true.
rules.risk: A map can ship with links pointing at the wrong lines.

sites.why: Files each wrongly placed link under warnings, never under failures.
Shows the same finding to the map builder as advice, so the check still passes.

rules.name: Split verdict confirms nothing
rules.statement: A stored link is judged out of date only when most reviewers agreed the claim it carries is true.
rules.risk: A single doubtful reading would move a link that was right all along.

sites.why: Skips a claim whose votes are tied or missing.
States that two reviewers cannot form a majority.

rules.name: Links that are never moved
rules.statement: A claim whose code link deliberately points at a declaration is never moved onto the line a reviewer read.
rules.risk: A record's link would slide off its definition onto one write line.

sites.why: Skips the comparison for a claim marked as report only.
Marks a claim about where records are kept as report only.
Refuses to write a correction for a kind of claim that has no movable link.

rules.name: Corrections stay in the parts' own code
rules.statement: A corrected code link is refused when it lands in a file that neither end of the relation claims.
rules.risk: A link could point into a third part's code.

sites.why: Refuses the correction and names the two parts whose files were checked.
Runs the refusal before any correction is written into the map.
Runs the same refusal when a recorded correction is replayed later.

rules.name: One written excuse, one claim
rules.statement: A person may excuse one code link a check called out. The note must quote the whole claim, then give the reason.
rules.risk: One short note could silence every finding about one part of the product.

sites.why: Accepts a written excuse only in the form that quotes a claim and gives a reason.
Drops exactly the one finding whose claim the note quotes.
